Looking at the folds: the octagon's center ends up at one corner of the triangle, the four "axis" vertices (top, bottom, left, right) at another corner, and the four "diagonal" vertices at the third corner (the left point in the last figure).

The cut removes the corner containing the diagonal vertices (NE, NW, SE, SW), with the cut line perpendicular to the octagon's edge. Since the cut crosses the fold line that bisects each of these vertices, unfolding produces a V‑shaped notch at each of the four diagonal vertices, while the axis vertices remain intact as protruding tabs.

This matches picture D: four notches at the diagonal positions and four intact "arms" at the top, right, bottom, and left.

\boxed{D}
